about: Five systems built the same way as Oracle7: no language model, every decision with a receipt, measured on held-out data once. Each is its own repository in the release; numbers are from each one's model card.

items.name: DeepSpace
items.does: Fault response for deep-space spacecraft. It reads telemetry, forms confirmed facts, then fault hypotheses, then admissible responses, each with a receipt. A self-maintenance gate admits rules learned from its own verified episodes.
measured: 98.9% correct on 1,700 fresh single-fault scenarios, 0 harmful actions (a limit-to-safe-mode baseline: 29.4%, 200 harmful)
9 learned rules admitted; all 4 planted wrong rules rejected
items.runs: Python standard library, a fraction of one CPU
items.use: spacecraft, satellites, any machine with telemetry and a fault table

items.name: Trafficcop
items.does: A decision service. Given a state and a set of options it returns one choice with a receipt: impossible options are struck, obligations are bound, attested outcomes rank the rest, and it abstains when nothing is warranted.
measured: 30 of 32 held-out routing decisions right (always-first: 8, random: 7)
about 0.1 ms per decision; it replaced a language-model decision service behind the same contract
items.use: routing work between tools, agents and specialists

items.name: Chameleon
items.does: Builds websites and components by reconstruction. Its operators are repair operations that act only when their preconditions hold, and a build counts as complete only when contracts written before it ran pass in a supervised browser.
measured: 0 false completions on held-out repositories (1 of 4 completed, 3 reported blocked with the reason)
13 complete / 13 blocked on dev and transfer runs
items.runs: Node and Python, a headless browser
items.use: the coding system of the family: site and component builds that prove themselves

items.name: Vision
items.does: Sees without trained weights. Fixed image descriptors are bound into one vector (HRR, D = 2048) and compared with stored, labelled examples; every answer cites the examples that voted, and it abstains when the vote is close. It reads text by rendering glyphs from open fonts.
measured: MNIST 98.58%, Fashion-MNIST 90.46%, CIFAR-10 62.99% (official test sets, run once)
items.use: checking images, reading screens and labels, verifying what Artist drew

items.name: Artist
items.does: Makes images by citation, with no generative model. A prompt is parsed into objects, counts, colours and positions; every object is a real photographed instance, cited by its image and annotation id; the layout satisfies the prompt by construction and Artist re-measures every clause from its own pixels.
measured: GenEval-style 50.9% on 2,212 held-out images, scored by an independent judge (an approximation of the official scorer)
items.use: stills for films and posts where every part has a source
